question.problem:
Find the value(s) of the constant $a$ that make the function $f(x)$ below continuous at $x=2.$
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14193886/assets/bee9ecfc2bcfaa7741ed1c2aca90b8a077c19715c2a642a9622856f986f434f3.svg)
question.worked_solution:
At $x=2,$ the left-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}(2x+a)^{2} \\  & =(2(2)+a)^{2} \\  & =(4+a)^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

 

and the right-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}({x}^{2}-3) \\  & =(2)^{2}-3 \\  & =4-3 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $f(x)$ to be continuous at $x=2,$ we require that

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}f(x) \\ (4+a)^{2} & =1 \\ \sqrt{(a+4)^{2}} & =\sqrt{1} \\ |a+4| & =1 \\ a+4 & =\pm 1 \\ a & =-4\pm 1 \\ a & =-5,-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=2$ for $a=-5$ or $a=-3.$
